purpose: Profile-and-fix record for the consumer-run tokenize stage on the pinned S02 corpus manifest, plus the residual full-corpus cost breakdown that T08 must plan against.
non_claims: not a full-corpus run result: no corpus-run artifact is superseded here
not a semantic, legal, authenticity or pagination claim
not a claim that the full 43785-entry run is feasible: this artifact records the opposite for the producer stages

allowed_edit_surface: behavior-preserving S04 edits (reader_composite / reading order), recorded in the task summary
forbidden: the five frozen upstream wire contracts
XML re-parse on the consumer read path
scope.untouched_after_edit: all 5 frozen wire contracts and all 8 immutability pins re-verified sha256-identical after the fix

removed_quadratics.was: tokenize_view rebuilt `segments_by_id` (a HashMap over the whole projection.segments vector) on every call, and tokenize_projection called it once per primary view: O(views x segments).
removed_quadratics.why_quadratic: a multi-paragraph document owns one primary view per paragraph, so a document with P paragraphs and S segments paid P*S hash-map inserts; the 10.8 MB entry has ~35359 paragraphs and ~36223 fragments, i.e. ~1.3e9 inserts.
removed_quadratics.fix: the lookup is now built once in tokenize_projection and shared by reference; the tokenize_view signature takes the shared map. External contracts and the composite-provenance semantics of section 5 are unchanged.

removed_quadratics.was: lookup linearly scanned self.views for the requested view id; tokenize_view calls reading_order(view) once per view: O(views^2).
removed_quadratics.why_quadratic: ~35359 views scanned per call and ~35359 calls -> ~1.25e9 id comparisons on the largest entry.
removed_quadratics.fix: added an additive `positions: HashMap<String, usize>` index built from self.views in ReadingOrderIndex::build; lookup is O(1) and returns exactly the same OrderedView or the same NotPrimaryView error. Behavior-preserving S04 edit, no observable change.

measurements.note: release build, M223_S07_TIMING per-stage wall time, one run per entry, single-file invocation of target/release/consumer-run --from-xml <pinned entry>. 'before' is the pre-fix binary (sha256 fa114a200fd436ad61a1c03fea44920f0a7920976a8c1286ae69e756532a06e3).

residual_for_t08.verdict: the tokenize-stage superlinearity is REMOVED within the allowed consumer surface; the full 43785-entry run is still not mechanically feasible in a practical budget, and the remaining cost is outside the frozen consumer API.
evidence: on the 29372660-byte entry the tokenize stage is now 34801 ms of a 245786 ms whole-file run (14%); capture+render_wire+read_wire+analyze+render_analysis is 180616 ms (73%) and graph import is 30365 ms (12%).
on the 5514930-byte entry analyze alone is 234063 ms of a 243511 ms run (96%) while tokenize is 3706 ms.

analyze is structure-dependent and non-monotonic in bytes (703267 -> 14263 ms, 1470360 -> 11052 ms, 3005188 -> 68799 ms, 5514930 -> 234063 ms, 10849143 -> 22745 ms, 29372660 -> 121737 ms), i.e. the same document family can be quadratic in fragments regardless of byte size.

at a conservative 5 s/entry average over 43785 entries the full run is ~60 h of wall time, and the largest entries cost 245 s each; the harness's bounded chunked --resume keeps it mechanically possible but not budget-feasible.
outside_consumer_surface: NpaGraph::import (npa_graph_projection) plus its mandatory second repeat-import pass
residual_for_t08.t08_recommendation: T08 must choose between a budget-bounded bounded-chunk publication (partial_is_not_full=true preserved) and the explicit section 8.1/9 boundary reassessment; the tokenize fix removes the consumer-side blocker but not the producer-side one.
